rulings.challenge_claim: Two recurrence claims that carry the close are asserted with no ref, tier or digit; the one digit given is attached to a form standing once book-wide that is nonetheless called a refrain; the tier-3 mark layer is routed into the substrate-signal keys; and a high confidence rests on a voice identification the morphology does not make.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on bytes, five ways. (i) The three-token form בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier) stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, byte tier, verses containing the three-token form) - the digit and its object are both right, and a form attested once cannot function as a refrain; the prose label and the refrain-shaped signal key both encode that error, and refrain-grade evidence is tier-1, so the mislabel is load-bearing. (ii) The claim that the opening petition repeats an earlier one carries no ref, no tier and no digit, although the byte ground is exact and available: רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier) stands verbatim in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier: Lam.1.11 and Lam.2.20). (iii) A parashah mark is named inside an observed-signal key, where the single-witness tier-3 disclosure belongs in prose only. (iv) The high confidence rests on assigning Lam.2.20-Lam.2.22 to the personified city, but its 1cs speaker and 2ms addressee are equally available to the poem's own narrator, whose 1cs already stands at עֵינַי֙ (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier) with 1cs verbs addressing the city at oshb:Lam.2.13; the forms do not separate the two (tier-1 speaker and addressee marking). (v) Both-sides law at the front seam: the imperative to pour out the heart before the Lord at Lam.2.19 and the prayer that answers it at Lam.2.20 bind across the cut, and the same divine title stands at Lam.2.19 and inside Lam.2.20 - undisclosed. REFINED: the challenge's supporting ground, that the close and the alef line share no attested spelling, is byte-false. The token בְּי֥וֹם is byte-identical at Lam.2.1 and Lam.2.22 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), each followed by an anger word - בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier) closing the alef line against בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier) closing the tav line. The wrath inclusio the reading asserts is real and citable at byte tier; the defect is that it is asserted at no level, not that it is wrong. Severity stays medium.
rulings.remedy: row.observed_substrate_signals: replace the refrain-shaped key for the day-of-anger form with a closure or inclusio key that asserts no recurrence, and delete the key naming the PE mark (the mark disclosure stays in row.device_notes prose). row.boundary_rationale: (a) drop the refrain word for the day-of-anger form while keeping its digit with the swept object named; (b) anchor the petition-recurrence sentence to oshb:Lam.1.11 and oshb:Lam.2.20 with the digit 'sweep: 2 verses, byte tier'; (c) anchor the wrath-inclusio sentence on the byte-tier token shared by Lam.2.1 and Lam.2.22 with the digit 'sweep: 2 verses, byte tier'. row.device_notes: add the front-seam both-sides disclosure (the imperative to pour out the heart before the Lord at Lam.2.19 against the prayer at Lam.2.20, and the divine title standing on both sides), and add one sentence recording that the forms do not separate the city's voice from the narrator's. row.confidence: high -> medium. TEST: every recurrence sentence in the row carries a ref, a named tier and a digit whose swept object and unit are stated; no signal key names a parashah mark; no form with a 1-verse sweep is called a refrain; the front-seam straddle is disclosed in-field.

rulings.challenge_claim: Every ground offered stands at or before the onset: the close at Lam.3.9 into Lam.3.10 carries no evidence and no disclosure although the same third-person affliction chain and the same 1cs-suffixed noun straddle it; the letter-order note is attached to letters the order does not touch; and the disclosure sentence characterises stretches of the poem outside this span.
rulings.grounds: Upheld at every point. (i) row.boundary_evidence_refs lists only the onset verse in both witnesses and the preceding poem's closing verse; nothing at all is offered at the close, while row.confidence stands at high - one of the row's own two seams carries no tier-1 ground. (ii) The chain is continuous across the cut: Lam.3.2-Lam.3.16 runs one pattern of third-person divine agency with 1cs object suffixes and no addressee anywhere, and the 1cs-suffixed noun דְּרָכַי֙ (oshb:Lam.3.9, byte tier) recurs as דְּרָכַ֥י (oshb:Lam.3.11, byte tier) immediately across the seam. TIER CORRECTION to the challenge: those two forms are not byte-identical (the accents differ), so the recurrence is not a byte-tier fact - it holds at accent-stripped tier (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.9, Lam.3.11) and at whole-token skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide: Lam.1.4, Lam.3.9, Lam.3.11, the first being a construct plural inside another phrase). At those tiers the straddle is real, and a device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity until it is disclosed. (iii) The letter-order note is byte-misattached: in this poem the swapped pair is the 16th and 17th letter set, standing at Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48 and Lam.3.49-Lam.3.51, far outside a span of the first three triplets, so the order fact is inoperative for alef, bet and gimel (tier-1 acrostic). (iv) The paseq sentence states what other spans of this poem disclose, which is not a property of this unit. The triplet-boundary cut itself stays permissible under the acrostic-boundary rule; what is missing is a ground for it. NEW FINDING, protective and in this span's favour: in this poem the parashah layer stands on triplet-closing verses only - 22 marked verses of 66 (sweep: 22 verses; the book-wide marked layer is 89 verses, 5 of them the distinct closing mark) - so the row's disclosure at Lam.3.3, Lam.3.6 and Lam.3.9 is already the complete in-span set for the symmetry arm and must not be completed to every verse in any repair.
rulings.remedy: row.boundary_evidence_refs: add at least one close-seam entry at oshb:Lam.3.9 or oshb:Lam.3.10, or state in row.boundary_rationale that the close rests on the triplet boundary alone. row.device_notes: disclose the straddle - the 1cs-suffixed noun for the speaker's ways stands at Lam.3.9 and again at Lam.3.11 (accent-stripped tier, sweep: 2 verses) and the third-person-agency chain with 1cs object suffixes runs on past the cut. row.boundary_rationale: delete the pe-before-ayin phrase from the alef/bet/gimel disclosure, or move it to the letter set it governs. row.device_notes: delete the clause reporting what other spans of this poem disclose, keeping only this span's own zero-paseq digit. row.confidence: high -> medium. Do NOT add per-verse parashah disclosures in this poem: the marked verses are the triplet closes only. TEST: both seams carry at least one verse-anchored ground; every straddling device named in the row carries its tier and its digit; no letter-order claim stands on a letter pair outside the 16th/17th set; no sentence in any field describes a stretch outside this span; the mark disclosure names exactly the triplet-closing verses of the span.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span is warranted by an unbroken voice across Lam.3.10-Lam.3.18, but Lam.3.17 carries a form that is second-person masculine or third-person feminine at the bytes and is read as direct address to the deity by the rendering, an ambiguity the grounds neither disclose nor resolve; splice extent and gloss extent do not match; and a whole-book superlative is carried with no digit.
rulings.grounds: Upheld. (i) Lam.3.17 opens וַתִּזְנַ֧ח (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier), a pointing common to a 2ms and a 3fs reading, with נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier) standing in the same verse as an available feminine subject; the rendering cited in this stretch takes the second-person reading. This is the only verse in Lam.3.10-Lam.3.18 where a second person can arise: every other affliction clause is third-person with a 1cs object suffix (oshb:Lam.3.11, oshb:Lam.3.12, oshb:Lam.3.15, oshb:Lam.3.16), with 1cs speech at oshb:Lam.3.14 and oshb:Lam.3.18. A same-voice warrant (tier-1 speaker marking) that never weighs the one verse capable of breaking it is incomplete, and the reading chosen bears on where this stretch begins. (ii) Extent: the closing splice וְתוֹחַלְתִּ֖י מֵיְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.18, byte tier) covers two words while the rendering paired with it covers four words of the verse - gloss extent must equal splice extent. (iii) The starkest-line-of-the-whole-lament wording is a whole-book superlative with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep and no byte-checkable object; superlative and exclusivity claims are never tier-dampened. Verified sound and to be preserved in any repair: the closing splice collates at byte tier, the paired rendering is verbatim, the dalet, he and vav triplets and their letters are correct, the triplet-closing marks at Lam.3.12, Lam.3.15 and Lam.3.18 are the complete in-span set, and the K/Q note at Lam.3.10 is disclosed by count with no slice taken there.
rulings.remedy: row.boundary_rationale: add one sentence disclosing that Lam.3.17 admits both a direct address to the deity and a statement about the speaker's own soul, and that the same-voice warrant is stated over the reading that keeps the third person; and either extend the closing splice to the whole clause the rendering covers or shorten the paired rendering to the two words actually spliced. row.boundary_rationale: replace the whole-book superlative with a non-exclusive description, or keep it only with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit. row.confidence: dent below medium only if the address reading is adopted. TEST: no superlative or exclusivity claim stands without an adjacent sweep digit naming object and unit; every splice's paired rendering covers the same words as the splice; the second-person-capable form inside the span is named in-field with its ambiguity stated.

rulings.challenge_claim: The chapter-wide singularity claimed for the turn at Lam.3.21 is contested by the bytes, since the same three-token turn stands again at Lam.3.24 inside the span and is left undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Upheld, and the severity raised from low to medium. עַל כֵּ֥ן אוֹחִֽיל (oshb:Lam.3.21, byte tier) recurs at Lam.3.24, where the same three tokens carry a prepositional phrase after them: עַל כֵּ֖ן אוֹחִ֥יל לֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.3.24, byte tier). The recurrence is skeleton tier, not byte tier - the accents differ - and stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier: Lam.3.21 and Lam.3.24). Naming Lam.3.21 the pivot line of the whole chapter is an exclusivity claim over a 66-verse poem carried with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, and the single byte fact bearing on it points the other way; exclusivity claims are never tier-dampened, which is why this is more than presentational. The omission also costs the span its best internal evidence on the one question it holds open: the twice-stated turn binds the zayin and het triplets to each other, which is exactly what a decision on whether Lam.3.19-Lam.3.24 belongs here would have to weigh, so the undisclosed repetition supports the span as drawn and is left unused. NEW FINDING on the same row, same class: the tet-triplet claim that all three verses open on the same word is untier-labelled. At byte tier that opening token stands in 2 verses (ט֤וֹב at oshb:Lam.3.25 and oshb:Lam.3.26, sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) and the third verse opens ט֣וֹב (oshb:Lam.3.27, byte tier); the three-verse figure is a whole-token skeleton-tier fact (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier: Lam.3.25-Lam.3.27) and must say so, since every recurrence claim carries its tier. Verified sound: all three splices collate at byte tier, all five renderings are verbatim, the letters and triplets are correct, the K/Q note at Lam.3.20 is disclosed by count with no slice taken there, and the disputed extent of the hope turn is held at a low setting with a frontier flag rather than decided.
rulings.remedy: row.boundary_rationale: replace the pivot-line-of-the-whole-chapter wording with a non-exclusive description, or keep an exclusivity claim only with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit; in the same field disclose the second site of the turn at Lam.3.24 with its tier and digit ('sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier') and weigh it as internal cohesion binding the zayin and het triplets under the held question. row.boundary_rationale: tier-label the tet-triplet opening-word claim as skeleton tier and keep its digit with the swept object named. TEST: no universal or superlative in the row stands without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; every recurrence sentence names its tier; the repeated turn at Lam.3.24 is present in the row; row.confidence and row.frontier_flag_considered remain as they are, since the held question is unchanged.

rulings.challenge_claim: First item: the span's own literature-type wording names a wisdom-style submission and compassion statement while its unit type names the hope reflection, with no one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure and an undented high confidence. Second item: the close is warranted by a shift into third-person argument, but both sides of Lam.3.33 into Lam.3.34 are third person at the bytes, and at the onset the antecedent of the three subjectless verbs is left one verse behind the seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Two DISTINCT defects, not one. The seam item is upheld on bytes: no 1cs and no 2ms form stands anywhere in Lam.3.28-Lam.3.39. Lam.3.28-Lam.3.30 are third-person yiqtol with third-person suffixes (יֵשֵׁ֤ב, oshb:Lam.3.28, byte tier); Lam.3.31-Lam.3.33 are three clauses of one conjunction about the Lord (אֲדֹנָֽי, oshb:Lam.3.31, byte tier); Lam.3.34-Lam.3.36 are three lamed-infinitives governed by אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א רָאָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.36, byte tier). No person, number, speaker or addressee changes across the stated seam, so the ground as written is not carried (tier-1 speaker and addressee marking); what changes is clause type, and the acrostic letter itself produces it - the kaf triplet forces the conjunction openers and the lamed triplet the infinitives - so it is not an independent signal. The onset item is upheld too: the three verbs have no expressed subject anywhere in the span and their nearest antecedent is לַגֶּ֔בֶר (oshb:Lam.3.27, byte tier), one verse behind the onset and undisclosed. Two supporting digits inside that item need correcting, since a reproduced digit with the wrong count-object is itself a defect: the adjacency of divine title immediately followed by the negative stands in 2 verses at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.36, Lam.3.37) and 3 at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, adding Lam.2.2, where the hit falls on the ketiv form of a K/Q verse), and it does not reach Lam.3.31 at all, where the negative precedes the title - so the continuity point holds on title-and-negative co-occurrence in both triplets, not on the adjacency figure cited beside it; and the five-verse consonantal figure belongs to the unprefixed string (sweep: 5 verses: Lam.1.16, Lam.3.1, Lam.3.27, Lam.3.35, Lam.3.39), while the prefixed form itself stands in 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, whole-token skeleton tier) - prefix tolerance is a per-length test, never a blind stripper. The classification item is REFINED rather than upheld: the divergence between the span's own literature-type wording and the category's defining content is real, and the stretch at Lam.3.34-Lam.3.39 treats the same divergence as disclosure-worthy while this span does not, an internal inconsistency sitting at an undented high confidence. But the framing that the content falls outside the category overstates it - the ruled vocabulary assigns that category to Lam.3.19-Lam.3.39 by extent, and this span sits wholly inside that stretch - so the cure is a disclosure and a confidence dent, not a category change. The triplet-boundary cut stays permissible; it needs a ground the bytes carry.
rulings.remedy: row.strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the person-or-register-shift ground with one the bytes carry - the triplet boundary plus the clause-type change, stated as letter-driven and therefore not an independent signal - or state plainly that the close rests on the triplet boundary alone. row.boundary_rationale: name the antecedent of the three subjectless verbs at Lam.3.27 and disclose that it stands one verse behind the onset. row.device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure for the submission-and-compassion content, in the same shape used at Lam.3.34-Lam.3.39, and vary the wording so no disclosure sentence converges into a shared 7-gram. row.confidence: high -> medium. Do NOT change row.unit_type: the ruled category covers Lam.3.19-Lam.3.39 by extent. TEST: no seam ground in the row asserts a person, number, speaker or addressee change that no form in the span carries; a letter-driven clause-type change is labelled as letter-driven; the operative-category deviation disclosure is present in device_notes; every digit in the row names its swept object, its unit and its tier, and any digit taken over a prefixed form is the per-length test rather than the bare string.

rulings.challenge_claim: The headline device, a pair of rhetorical questions in succession at the close, is not what the bytes carry: the two interrogative-marked lines are separated by a verse whose question status exists only in the rendering; the stated ketiv/qere scope is narrower than the quoting actually done; and the onset repeats a contrast the bytes do not carry.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the adjacency, refined on the count and on the onset. Lam.3.37 opens מִ֣י זֶ֤ה (oshb:Lam.3.37, byte tier) and Lam.3.39 opens מַה יִּתְאוֹנֵן֙ (oshb:Lam.3.39, byte tier); between them Lam.3.38 opens מִפִּ֤י עֶלְיוֹן֙ לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֔א (oshb:Lam.3.38, byte tier) and carries no interrogative particle at all, so the words in succession are byte-false, and the question-pair signal key encodes that error into the taxonomy (tier-1 discourse frame misdescribed). REFINED: the count itself is not wrong once its object is named - lines opening with an interrogative particle inside the mem triplet stand in exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.37 and Lam.3.39) - so the cure is the adjacency word and the missing object, not the digit. What raises this above presentation is the point the challenge makes exactly: the rendering reads the intervening verse as a question too, so a question count taken from the translation returns three, and translation punctuation is never-evidence, so a device count that moves with it cannot corroborate a close. Also upheld: the ketiv/qere sentence says the splice stops short of the variant word, which is true of the splice but understates the engagement, because the rendering quoted for that verse follows the qere plural rather than the ketiv singular; and an original-language ref is listed at Lam.3.39 with no Hebrew engagement anywhere at that verse. REFINED: the onset's stated turn into third-person argument does not mark a person change, since Lam.3.28-Lam.3.33 is already third person throughout - but the row's own next clause states that register continuity accurately, so this is a phrasing correction, not a second seam defect. Verified sound: the opening splice collates at byte tier, both renderings are verbatim, the lamed and mem triplets and their letters are correct, the triplet-closing marks at Lam.3.36 and Lam.3.39 are the complete in-span set, the cohortative reading of the following triplet is byte-true, and the one-sentence category deviation is disclosed as required. Severity raised from low to medium: a byte-false device carries the close's rationale and is encoded as a signal key, and the ketiv/qere scope understatement is an independent defect on the same row.
rulings.remedy: row.boundary_rationale: delete the words in succession and state the object of the two-count explicitly (lines opening with an interrogative particle inside the mem triplet, sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.37 and Lam.3.39), adding that the intervening verse carries no interrogative particle in the source even though its rendering is a question. row.observed_substrate_signals: rename the question-pair key so it asserts no adjacency. row.device_notes: correct the ketiv/qere sentence to say that the Hebrew splice does not reach the variant word while the quoted rendering of that verse follows the qere. row.boundary_evidence_refs: either add a byte-tier splice from Lam.3.39 to the row or drop oshb:Lam.3.39 from the list. row.boundary_rationale: reword the onset contrast so it names a clause-type and topic change rather than implying a person change. TEST: no device claim in the row depends on the rendering's punctuation; every count names its swept object and unit; every original-language ref in boundary_evidence_refs has Hebrew engagement at that verse; the ketiv/qere disclosure covers the quoted rendering as well as the splice.
